title: The globular star cluster NGC 6752

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This view from the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope's Wide Field Imager at La Silla shows NGC 6752, a globular star cluster in the southern constellation Pavo, the Peacock, about 14,000 light-years away.

Globular clusters are dense, ball-shaped groups of old stars held together by gravity. Because their stars formed at roughly the same time, they are natural laboratories for testing ideas about how stars age and die.

NGC 6752 delivered a surprise. Studies of the cluster with ESO's Very Large Telescope unexpectedly showed that many of its stars do not go through a phase of mass loss at the end of their lives. Ageing stars are generally expected to shed material into space as they near the end, so the finding challenges the standard picture of how such stars finish their lives.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (32.60 x 31.82 arcminutes) and distance (14000 light years), the frame spans roughly 133 × 130 light-years. Its light set out about 14,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.eye: Long camera exposures gather far more light than the eye can, revealing individual stars across the cluster.
